name: sindhubhairavi
notes: Bhashanga; listed as janya of 8 (Hanumatodi) by Wikipedia and karnatik.com (some older texts place it under 20 Natabhairavi or 10 Natakapriya). Uses R2 in aroha and R1 in avaroha; in light/bhajan music virtually all 12 notes appear (G3, D2, N3 as anya swaras) - matching should be lenient. Wikipedia list gives vakra aroha S R2 G2 M1 G2 P D1 N2 S. DISAGREEMENT: the Wikipedia Sindhu Bhairavi page (Hindustani notation) gives S r g m g P d n S / N d P m g r S n S - komal re ascending and shuddha ni at the top of the descent; the Carnatic table uses R2 ascending. Both re and N3 are therefore expected in songs.
western: Phrygian/Aeolian blend - natural minor with b2 descending; chromatic in practice - degrees 1 b2 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7
mood: pathos, devotion; very common for bhajans and closing pieces

name: bhairavi
notes: Bhashanga: D2 (chatushruti dha) in aroha is an anya swara relative to parent 20; D1 in avaroha. Common vakra aroha S G2 R2 G2 M1 P D2 N2 S (Wikipedia list). NOT the same as Hindustani Bhairavi (all komal) - see 'hindustanibhairavi'. Bare alias 'bhairavi' assigned here (Carnatic); a Hindi-language bhajan labelled 'Bhairavi' most likely means the Hindustani raga.
hindustani_equiv: no exact equivalent (NOT Hindustani Bhairavi); closest Asavari/Jaunpuri with shuddha dha ascending
western: natural minor with raised 6th ascending (Dorian up, Aeolian down) - degrees 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 6 b7

name: anandabhairavi

hindustani_equiv: no exact equivalent; Kafi-thaat light ragas (Pilu-like phrases)

The Wikipedia Shuddha Dhanyasi infobox writes S G1 M1 P N1 S, which contradicts its own parent (Kharaharapriya) and karnatik.com - treated as a page error.

name: abheri

Karnataka Devagandhari is often equated with Abheri, but karnatik.com lists it as a separate 28 janya (with G3), so it is not used as an alias.
western: minor pentatonic up, Dorian down - degrees 1 2 b3 4 5 6 b7

notes: Hindustani Desh (Wikipedia): ascent 'N S R, M P N, S', descent 'S n D, P D M G R, P M G, R G N S'. Carnatic Desh (janya 28, Wikipedia table): S R2 M1 P N3 S / S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S. Same raga; N3 up, N2 down.
hindustani_equiv: Desh (Carnatic Desh / close to Kedaragowla + Surati)
western: Mixolydian down, major 7 up (major/Mixolydian mix) - degrees 1 2 3 4 5 6 b7 7

name: khamaj
notes: Own entry (not an alias of Harikambhoji): Khamaj raga uses N3 ascending and N2 descending, R omitted ascending. 'khamaj thaat' is an alias of mela 28.

name: yaman
notes: Wikipedia infobox gives full S R G M2 P D N S; S and P are commonly skipped in ascent (N R G M2 D N S). 'Yaman Kalyan' adds shuddha ma in descent (ex pc 5).

name: basant
notes: Wikipedia: ascent S G M2 d N S, descent S N d P M2 G, M2 G r S. Characteristic leap M2 d1 to upper r1 S; shuddha ma occurs in some phrases (ex pc 5). NOT Carnatic Vasantha (see 'vasantha').
carnatic_equiv: Kamavardhini family (no exact Carnatic raga; unrelated to Carnatic Vasantha)
hindustani_equiv: Kamavardhini family (no exact Carnatic raga; unrelated to Carnatic Vasantha)

name: pahadi
notes: Light/folk raga, usually rendered with the tonic feel shifted (much movement around lower P and D). Scale from the Wikipedia janya table / karnatik.com (Pahadi, 29: S R2 G3 P D2 P D2 S / N3 D2 P G3 M1 G3 R2 S N3 D2 P D2 S). Komal ni and other accidentals appear freely in light music (ex pc 10).
western: major pentatonic ascent; major scale descent - degrees 1 2 3 4 5 6 7

name: maand
notes: Rajasthani folk raga (e.g. 'Kesariya balam'); phrases are vakra, and komal ni appears in many renditions (ex pc 10). Scale from the Wikipedia janya table ('Mand Hindustani', 29: S G3 M1 D2 N3 S / S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S); karnatik.com (Carnatic Mand, 29) gives aroha S G3 M1 P D2 S with the same avaroha - same pcs.
western: major scale with folk turns - degrees 1 2 3 4 5 6 7

name: bhairav
notes: Komal re and komal dha are sung with slow oscillation (andolan).
western: double harmonic major (Byzantine) - degrees 1 b2 3 4 5 b6 7

name: miyankitodi
notes: Hindustani Todi (Wikipedia): P omitted ascending. The bare alias 'todi' is assigned to Carnatic Hanumatodi (mela 8), which is a different scale.
western: Phrygian #4 with major 7th - degrees 1 b2 b3 #4 5 b6 7

name: puriyadhanashri
notes: Wikipedia: P skipped ascending.
western: double harmonic major with #4 - degrees 1 b2 3 #4 5 b6 7

name: purvi
notes: Uses both ma (shuddha ma in descent G M1 G). The Carnatic raga Poorvi (janya 15, S R1 G3 M1 P D1 N3, Wikipedia table and karnatik) is a different raga that shares the name.
western: double harmonic with #4 and natural 4 descending - degrees 1 b2 3 4 #4 5 b6 7

name: marwa
notes: No P. Same pitch set as Puriya, Sohini and Carnatic Hamsanandi - distinguished by emphasis (Marwa centres on komal re and dha).

name: sohini
notes: Komal re only in descent; upper register emphasis.

name: lalit
notes: No P; uses both ma consecutively (M1 M2 M1 G). DISAGREEMENT: Bhatkhande classified Lalit under Marwa thaat with shuddha dha; modern practice and Wikipedia/tanarang use komal dha (Purvi). Komal dha used here; shuddha dha may appear in some gharanas.

sources.note: scale given as plain text; compared by hand: tanarang scale quoted in article body

name: kedar
notes: Both ma; shuddha ma dominant, tivra ma in M2 P. Wikipedia: ascent S M G P D N S, descent S N D P M2 P M1 R S. tanarang omits ga from the formal scale (S M P D N S / S N D P, M P D P, m m R S) but describes ga as a touch in m G P; ga kept here. Distinct from Carnatic Kedaram and Kedaragowla. The Wikipedia janya-table row for Kedar is garbled and was ignored.
western: major scale with both 4 and #4 - degrees 1 2 3 4 #4 5 6 7

name: brindavanisarang
notes: No ga, no dha; N3 up, N2 down (Wikipedia).
carnatic_equiv: Brindavana Saranga (Carnatic adds a ga touch); Madhyamavati is the N2-only form
hindustani_equiv: Brindavana Saranga (Carnatic adds a ga touch); Madhyamavati is the N2-only form

name: madhuvanti
western: Lydian diminished (melodic minor with #4) - degrees 1 2 b3 #4 5 6 7

name: pilu
notes: Light raga with both ga and both ni. Sources differ in detail: Wikipedia page S g m P N S / S N D P m G m P g R S (shuddha ni in descent); tanarang S G m P N S / S n D P m g R S (komal ni in descent); the Wikipedia janya table lists both forms of ga, dha and ni. The union of the two raga pages is used; komal dha also occurs (ex pc 8).
western: Dorian / major mix; chromatic in light music - degrees 1 2 b3 3 4 5 6 b7 7

name: jaijaiwanti
notes: Both ga and both ni (Wikipedia Dwijavanti/Jaijaivanti page). Carnatic Dwijavanti (janya 28) is the counterpart; it has its own entry (dwijavanthi). karnatik.com lists jaijaivanti only as a 28 janya without G2/N3 in its formal scale (S R2 G3 M1 P D2 N2), though both are heard in practice.
western: major/Mixolydian mix with b3 grace - degrees 1 2 b3 3 4 5 6 b7 7

name: dhani
notes: tanarang: S g m P n S / S n P m g S (pure minor pentatonic); Wikipedia adds R only as a touch before S in descent ((R)S) - kept as ex pc 2. Same notes as Shuddhadhanyasi.

name: tilakkamod
notes: Wikipedia: 'P N S R G S, R M P N S / S P D M G, S R G S N'. Shuddha ni dominant; komal ni occasionally in light music (ex pc 10).
western: major scale with zig-zag phrases - degrees 1 2 3 4 5 6 7

name: kalavati
notes: Hindustani Kalavati (Wikipedia). CAUTION: Carnatic 'Kalavati' (janya 16, Wikipedia table: S R1 M1 P D2 S) is a different raga; the Carnatic raga with these notes is Valaji.

name: megh
notes: Wikipedia: ascent S m R m P n S, descent S n P m R m n R S. No ga, no dha (Megh Malhar adds a komal-ga touch).

name: meghmalhar
notes: Malhar-anga phrase M R P. DISAGREEMENT: Wikipedia infobox lists S R P m P n (d) N S' / S' n P m R g~ m R S (komal-ga kan, dha and shuddha ni touches); many musicians treat Megh and Megh Malhar as the same S R M P n scale. Extra touches recorded as ex pcs 3, 9, 11.

sources.note: scale given as plain text; compared by hand: core S R M P n agrees; page adds g kan, (d) and N touches - kept as extra_pcs

name: shuddhasarang
notes: No ga; both ma. Matches tanarang (,N S R M P N S / S N D P M P M m R S). No Wikipedia page; karnatik.com's 'sudda saarang' is an unrelated Carnatic raga.

name: gorakhkalyan
notes: No ga. DISAGREEMENT on P: tanarang omits P entirely (S R m D S / S n D m R S); Wikipedia includes P in descent (S n D P M R S). P treated as a weak extra note (ex pc 7).
carnatic_equiv: close to Carnatic Andolika / Madhyamavati family
hindustani_equiv: close to Carnatic Andolika / Madhyamavati family

sources.note: scale given as plain text; compared by hand: page includes P; kept as extra_pcs

name: hamsanadam
notes: janya of Neetimati (60)

name: sri
notes: janya of Kharaharapriya (22); D2 and g2 only in avaroha
western: Dorian-flavoured: 1 2 4 5 b7 up, 1 b7 6 5 4 2 b3 2 down

name: mohanakalyani
notes: janya of Mechakalyani (65)

name: vasantabhairavi
notes: janya of Vakulabharanam (14)
western: Phrygian dominant (5th mode of harmonic minor)

name: dwijavanthi
notes: Carnatic counterpart of Hindustani Jaijaiwanti. Bhashanga: G2 (sadharana ga) in the descent (R2 g2 R2 S) and N3 (kakali ni) as anya swaras (N3 not in the formal scale, ex pc 11). Wikipedia and karnatik.com give the same scale; karnatik.com also has a separate 'jujAvanti' entry (S R2 G3 M1 P D2 S N2 D2 N2 S / S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S R2 M1 G3 R2 S) without G2, which Wikipedia treats as the same raga.
western: Mixolydian with a b3 grace in the descent (and an occasional 7) - degrees 1 2 b3 3 4 5 6 b7

name: revagupti
notes: Audava-audava janya of Mayamalavagowla (15); no ma, no ni. Morning raga. Differs from Bhoopalam only in ga (G3 here, G2 in Bhoopalam).
western: pentatonic 1 b2 3 5 b6 (double harmonic scale without 4 and 7) - degrees 1 b2 3 5 b6

name: manirangu
notes: Janya of Kharaharapriya (22): ga only in the descent, no dha. Close to Sri ragam and to Madhyamavati with g2 added in the descent.
western: 1 2 4 5 b7 going up, adds b3 coming down (Dorian without 6) - degrees 1 2 b3 4 5 b7

name: mishrashivaranjani
notes: Light-music (mishra) Shivaranjani: the Shivaranjani pentatonic plus shuddha/antara ga (G3), touched in the descent just before g2. DISAGREEMENT on the extra notes: karnatik.com adds only G3 (avaroha S D2 P G3 G2 R2 S); the Wikipedia janya list keeps the plain Shivaranjani scale and lists anya swaras R1 G3 M1 M2 D1 N2 N3 (i.e. almost any note can appear in film/light renditions). Only G3, which both sources agree on, is recorded in the scale; the rest are deliberately not put in extra_pcs so this entry does not become a catch-all.
western: minor pentatonic with major 6th (1 2 b3 5 6) plus a major 3rd touched coming down - degrees 1 2 b3 3 5 6

sources.note: anya swaras listed: R1 G3 M1 M2 D1 N2 N3

name: nagaswaravali
notes: Audava-audava janya of Harikambhoji (28); no ri, no ni (so it fits Shankarabharanam just as well).

name: rageshri
notes: Hindustani Rageshree, Khamaj thaat: pa varjya throughout, ri only in the descent, komal ni. Like Bageshri but with shuddha ga. tanarang.com: 'S' n D m G R S' is also used in the descent, and the literature allows both ni but performers use komal ni (shuddha ni rarely, ex pc 11); a 'Pancham-Rageshree' variant with pa is rarely heard. DISAGREEMENT: karnatik.com gives N3 in the aroha (S G3 M1 D2 N3 S); Wikipedia (raga page and janya list) and tanarang give komal ni, the list marking N3 as rare.
carnatic_equiv: Rageshri (karnatik.com lists it as a 28 harikambhoji janya)
western: Mixolydian without the 5th: 1 3 4 6 b7 up, 2 only coming down - degrees 1 2 3 4 6 b7

sources.note: N3 listed as a rare anya swara

name: purnachandrika
notes: Vakra sampurna janya of Dheerasankarabharanam (29): dha only ascending (P D2 P S), ni only descending (S N3 P), zigzag R G M R in the descent. Close to Janaranjani.
western: major scale (Ionian) with zigzag phrases; 6 only going up, 7 only coming down - degrees 1 2 3 4 5 6 7

name: janasammodini
notes: Shadava janya of Harikambhoji (28): Mohanam plus kaisiki ni (no ma). karnatik.com also lists a second, different 'jana sammOdhini' under 25 Mararanjani (S R2 G3 P D1 S / S D1 P G3 R2 S); Wikipedia gives only the 28 version, used here.
western: major pentatonic with b7 - degrees 1 2 3 5 6 b7

sources.note: different raga with the same name; not used

name: narayani
notes: Janya of Harikambhoji (28): no ga at all; ni (komal) only in the descent. The Hindustani raag Narayani (Khamaj thaat) has the same notes.
western: Mixolydian without the 3rd; b7 only coming down - degrees 1 2 4 5 6 b7

name: shyamkalyan
notes: Kalyan thaat: tivra ma (M2) ascending (R M P N S'), shuddha ma (M1) in the 'G m P G m R S' phrase; dha varjya in the aroha; ga avoided in a straight ascent. A Kalyan-Kamod blend. tanarang.com and the Wikipedia janya list give the same aroha/avaroha.
western: Lydian with the natural 4th also used (both 4ths); no 6 going up - degrees 1 2 3 4 #4 5 6 7

name: chenchurutti
notes: Janya of Harikambhoji (28), sung mostly in the middle and lower octave: the range runs from mandra D2 up to madhya n2 (nishadantya-type), so the written aroha starts on the lower dha. Wikipedia lists G2 as an occasional anya swara (ex pc 3); karnatik.com does not. ragasurabhi.com confirms the alias chenjurutti and parent 28 (no scale given) and notes it is sung in madhyama shruti.
western: Mixolydian, sung low (from the 6th below Sa up to b7) - degrees 1 2 3 4 5 6 b7

sources.note: anya swara G2
janya of 28; no scale given

name: malahari
notes: Janya of Mayamalavagowla (15): ga only in the descent, no ni (so it also fits melas 13/14). Beginner raga of the Purandara Dasa geetams.
western: 1 b2 4 5 b6 going up, adds 3 coming down (double harmonic without 7) - degrees 1 b2 3 4 5 b6

name: gaudmalhar
notes: Bilawal thaat with both ni: shuddha ni ascending (m P D N S'), komal ni descending, plus the Malhar phrase m R P. Wikipedia (after Bor, The Raga Guide) gives avaroha S' D n P M G M R S; tanarang.com gives S' n D n P m G R G (R)S. Same notes, slightly different phrasing. Not the Carnatic Gowdamalhar (S R2 M1 P D2 S / S N3 M1 G3 R2 S), which is a different raga.
western: major scale with a b7 also used coming down (both 7ths) - degrees 1 2 3 4 5 6 b7 7

name: miyanmalhar
notes: Kafi thaat. Both ni (komal ni before dha, shuddha ni rising to Sa); komal ga oscillates in the descent (g m R S).
western: Dorian with a major 7 rising to the octave - degrees 1 2 b3 4 5 6 b7 7

name: hamsavinodini
notes: Janya of 29 Dheerasankarabharanam without Pa.

name: navarasakannada
notes: Janya of 28 Harikambhoji: S G M P S up, S N D M G R S down.
western: Mixolydian, skipping notes going up - degrees 1 2 3 4 5 6 b7

name: hamirkalyani
notes: Janya of 65 Mechakalyani with shuddha ma in the descent; the Carnatic form of Hindustani Kedar.
western: major scale with both 4 and #4 - degrees 1 2 3 4 #4 5 6 7

name: bahudari
notes: Janya of 28 Harikambhoji without Ri (and without Dha going down).

name: mandari
notes: Janya of 51 Kamavardhini (Pantuvarali) without Dha.

name: nayakikanada
notes: Kafi thaat, Kanada family: no Dha; the Kanada turn g m R S in the descent.
western: Dorian without the 6th - degrees 1 2 b3 4 5 b7
